steps.text: NA-0764 (D-1405; desktop D-0041) -- THE CONTACTS SURFACE. Instruments I1', I2', I3, I4-behaviour, I5, I6' and I8. ⚠ THE DESKTOP HARNESS HAS NO FIXTURE RELAY (ENG-0226, open), so nothing here completes a real handshake. The auto-connect PATH is proven against the engine on a real loopback relay at qsl-protocol's na0764_m3_empty_slot_accept; end to end it is proven only by the operator's two-machine flight. What IS driven here is every decision the front end makes, with its inputs planted.
A vault, so the run reaches an unlocked surface where the Contacts pane lives.

THE PANE OPENS FROM THE RAIL. Before Lane C this button revealed a stub note; it now opens a real surface, and the retired revealer is sealed at design_polish.rs.

⚠⚠ SUPERSEDE ANY IN-FLIGHT REFRESH BEFORE PLANTING, AND SAY WHY. `showContactsPane()` fires an async `refreshContacts()` that awaits real IPC, so it resolves AFTER the planting step below. The first version of this scenario raced exactly there: planted rows were asserted PRESENT and were gone two steps later. That was the PRODUCT racing (cold read C-12), and it is now cured in main.js by a generation guard. Bumping the generation here is how the test uses that same cure to make its own setup deterministic, rather than hoping the timing holds.

steps.script: window.__na0764 = { realRefresh: refreshContacts }; contactsRefreshGen += 1; refreshContacts = function(){ return Promise.resolve(); }; return 'refresh-held';

steps.text: ⚠ AND THE STUB IS STILL SILENT. Opening the pane must not reveal the message that said the pane did not exist.

I3 -- STATES RENDER, ALL SIX, per ruling R4's table. The rows and statuses are PLANTED so every state is reachable: a real rig cannot produce a CHANGED peer or a storage fault on demand. Each assertion reads the state the RENDERER chose, not the input it was given.

steps.script: contactsRows = [{alias:'dana', display_name:null, blocked:false, state:'PINNED', fingerprint:{full:'a'.repeat(64), voice:'849301265709214773805516209447'}, device_count:1},{alias:'aud', display_name:null, blocked:false, state:'PINNED', fingerprint:null, device_count:1},{alias:'aliza', display_name:null, blocked:false, state:'UNVERIFIED', fingerprint:null, device_count:1},{alias:'marcus', display_name:null, blocked:false, state:'CHANGED', fingerprint:null, device_count:1},{alias:'pat', display_name:null, blocked:false, state:'UNVERIFIED', fingerprint:null, device_count:1},{alias:'oldpeer', display_name:null, blocked:true, state:'CHANGED', fingerprint:null, device_count:1}];contactsStatus = {dana:{state:'active',reason:'handshake'}, aud:{state:'active',reason:'handshake'},aliza:{state:'inactive',reason:'missing_seed'}, marcus:{state:'active',reason:'handshake'},pat:{state:'inactive',reason:'unsafe_parent'}, oldpeer:{state:'active',reason:'handshake'}};contactsNewBadge.clear(); contactsNewBadge.add('dana');contactsOutstanding = 0; renderContactsList(); renderContactDetail();return String(document.querySelectorAll('.contact-row').length);

steps.text: ⚠⚠ THE ARM THIS LANE EXISTS FOR: `missing_seed` renders CONNECTING, never a fault. The desktop never sets QSC_QSP_SEED, so this is what EVERY not-yet-connected contact answers. Classifying it as a fault would ship 'This connection has a storage problem' on the commonest state in the app and would leave Connecting... with no reachable member at all.
And a genuine structural fault DOES render as a fault -- so the arm above is a classification, not a blanket.
CHANGED dominates Active (R4): the peer-key-changed signal is the MITM tell and an Active session must not bury it.
And blocked dominates CHANGED (R4).
The verify-first badge outranks plain Connected -- an auto-created contact must not look settled before anyone compared a code.
THE ROW WORD IS THE BLESSED COPY, read as RENDERED.
I8 -- THE BADGE CLEARS ON OPEN, and the ack is IN MEMORY ONLY (ruling sec 5 forbids new persistence for it).
And the row leaves the new state, so the nudge is genuinely spent rather than merely un-flagged.

THE DETAIL RENDERS THE RATIFIED TIER-1 CODE: 30 digits in 6 groups of 5. ⚠ The blessed mockup showed 'QF3K-92MB-7A', which is NEITHER ratified tier and about half the display strength; it was a placeholder, and the ratified voice form is what ships (STOP 002 D-B).
I6' -- THE OUTSTANDING HINT AT 0 / 1 / n. At ZERO the line is hidden rather than reading '0 invites'.

I4 BEHAVIOUR -- THE FOOTER'S PRECEDENCE, WITH THE CORRECTED RED ARM (cold read C-08). The obvious arm -- an unknown reason in the QUIET case -- passes even when the chain is wrong, because the defect only shows under trouble. The arm that matters is an unknown reason WHILE the tick is in trouble: the please-report tripwire must still win.
Storage and locked likewise outrank an outage -- and an outage and a storage fault are CORRELATED, both following a bad restart or a moved vault, so this is the case that actually happens.
The outage arm renders ONLY in the otherwise-Ready case -- which is exactly where it belongs.

steps.text: I1'/I2' -- THE AUTO-CONNECT CLASS DECIDES CORRECTLY. `invoke` is stubbed so the class's INPUTS are planted and its CALLS are recorded; the relay itself is out of reach here (ENG-0226) and is measured in qsl-protocol instead. The recorded calls are the instrument.

steps.script: window.__na0764 = { calls: [], realInvoke: invoke };invoke = function(cmd, args) { window.__na0764.calls.push({cmd: cmd, args: args}); if (cmd === 'relay_config_get') return Promise.resolve({relay_url: 'https://r.example:8443'}); if (cmd === 'invite_list') return Promise.resolve([  {invite_id:'inv-active', state:'active', expiry: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)+3600, label:'Matt2'},  {invite_id:'inv-revoked', state:'revoked', expiry: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)+3600, label:'Gone'},  {invite_id:'inv-redeemed', state:'redeemed', expiry: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)+3600, label:'Done'},  {invite_id:'inv-expired', state:'active', expiry: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)-10, label:'Old'},  {invite_id:'inv-nolabel', state:'active', expiry: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)+3600, label:null}]); if (cmd === 'invite_accept') return Promise.resolve(null); return Promise.resolve(null); };return 'stubbed';

steps.text: I1' -- EXACTLY ONE accept, and it is the ACTIVE, UNEXPIRED, LABELLED invite.
⚠ AND THE ALIAS IS THE INVITE'S OWN LABEL (R1), not the invite id. Passing the id would provision a contact named after a routing token.
I2' -- A REVOKED INVITE'S SLOT IS NEVER ACCEPTED. Nor is a redeemed one, nor an expired one. This is the arm that keeps a killed code from being quietly re-honoured by the tick.

⚠ THE UNLABELLED INVITE IS SKIPPED AND COUNTED, NOT SILENTLY DROPPED. The mint's own caption calls the label OPTIONAL, so a blessed GUI flow produces invites with no alias to provision under. The tally makes the gap observable; its disposition is the operator's and is declared at STOP 2.
An EMPTY slot is a no-op: nobody redeemed, so nothing finished and no badge was minted. This is the case the tick meets on almost every beat.

I5 -- REFRESH ON A SCAN THAT CHANGED STATE, and ONLY then. The refresh is observed through a counter on the real render path rather than by watching the DOM, so the arm cannot pass on an unrelated repaint.

steps.script: window.__na0764.renders = 0; refreshContacts = function(){ window.__na0764.renders += 1; return Promise.resolve(); };recordScanOutcome({source:'tick',at:Date.now()},{why:'tick',scanned:1,finished:0,pending:1,attempted:1,failed:0,unlabelled:0});return String(window.__na0764.renders);
